newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai leadership change will boost stocks - poll.
newsitem.headline: Thai leadership change will boost stocks - poll.

text.p: Investors in Thailand believe that a change in the country's political leadership will boost the stock market, an informal newspaper survey said on Tuesday.

A Bangkok Post poll said more than half the 122 Thai investors surveyed thought the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) index would rise sharply over the next six months if there was a leadership change. Nearly 35 percent of the 29 foreign investors polled agreed, and 48 percent said the SET would rise slightly.

When asked what would happen over the next six months if the current leadership remained in place, 42 percent of the Thais and 41 percent of the foreigners said the market would fall sharply. Another 39 percent of the Thais and 45 percent of the foreigners predicted a slight drop.
Last week the SET tumbled to three-year lows. It has recouped some of the loss over the past few trading days as support funds boosted the market.
The poll was published a day before Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa was to face a no-confidence debate in parliament.

The motion, tabled by the opposition, claims that Banharn has damaged the country through mismanagement and inefficiency. It accuses him of incompetence, economic mismanagement and plagiarism involving his master's thesis.
Banharn has denied the accusations and has said he will not step down.

Political uncertainty, coupled with a lack of investor confidence in the government's ability to control the slowing economy and a rising current account deficit, has caused a downward spiral in the SET index in recent months.
In the Post poll, 36 percent of the investors surveyed said the SET's poor performance was due to political uncertainty and 31 pecent said it was due to a decline in macroeconomic factors.
